headline: On November 21, 2004: Paris Club writes off 80% of Iraq's debt
captionCards: Set precedent for post-conflict debt relief
instagramCaption:
Paris Club wipes out 80% of Iraq’s external debt.


The Paris Club agreed to write off up to $100 billion in Iraq’s debt in 2004. This decision involved major creditor nations working through the informal group established in 1956. The move aimed to support Iraq’s economic recovery after conflict. A key detail: the write-off capped at $100 billion, not unlimited.

This set a precedent for large-scale debt relief in post-conflict nations.
